thesis: ASML remains structurally supply-constrained on AI-driven EUV demand: JPMorgan reported (Sept 14) that most new EUV orders now target 2028 delivery, ASML is nearly sold out for 2027, and Intel/Samsung both expanded High-NA EUV production commitments through early September. The Sept 14 sector-wide selloff (-6%, triggered by Anthropic CEO's call to slow AI development pace, which hit all semicap names) knocked the stock off its highs, but that was a sector/macro event rather than an ASML-specific deterioration, and shares have partly recovered since on company-specific demand confirmations (Samsung High-NA DRAM partnership, Intel 1M-wafer milestone). No confirmed earnings print or other binary catalyst is due before the next review.
invalidation: A confirmed pullback in hyperscaler/foundry capex commitments (e.g., TSMC or Samsung EUV order cuts) or a Q3 print that misses the raised FY26 guidance (43-45B EUR sales).

invalidation: A Q3 print or guidance revision that reverses the raised FY26 outlook, or a reversal of the recent analyst upgrade cycle.

thesis: NVO's US-listed shares fell ~8% Monday on very heavy volume (4.7x average) after its Capital Markets Day unveiled long-term targets (150B DKK risk-adjusted pipeline sales by 2035, 5+ new multi-blockbusters by 2030) that the market read as underwhelming given semaglutide's 2032 US patent cliff and the already-lost China exclusivity; separately, the Financial Times reported shareholders are pushing management to diversify via M&A away from GLP-1 dependence. The same-day disclosure that investigational CagriSema beat Eli Lilly's tirzepatide in two Phase 3 trials (12.4% vs 9.1% weight loss, and 21.0% vs 2.0% placebo) is the strongest bullish counter-evidence, but it doesn't change the read because management's own framing centered on defending share through the post-patent-cliff transition rather than expanding the total opportunity, and the stock sold off anyway despite the trial win being disclosed same-day.
invalidation: A subsequent clarification or analyst consensus that the 2035 targets were conservative/sandbagged, or confirmed M&A activity that credibly diversifies revenue away from semaglutide.

thesis: WBD jumped ~10-11% to a fresh 52-week high on ~12.5x average volume after Paramount Skydance reached a settlement (announced Monday) with a 12-state attorney-general coalition led by California's Rob Bonta, resolving the main legal obstacle that had blocked Paramount's ~$110B acquisition of WBD since a multistate lawsuit was filed earlier this year. This is a confirmed, already-reached settlement (not a rumor), but it is explicitly described as "subject to court approval," so the deal isn't fully closed — that pending-approval step, plus the fact that Paramount's own stock rose far less than WBD's on the news (raising a question about how much of the settlement cost is being absorbed by Paramount vs. reflected in WBD's take-out value), keeps this from clearing the high bar despite the size of the move.
invalidation: Court rejection or material renegotiation of the settlement terms, or a new legal challenge to the merger from a party not covered by this settlement.

thesis: NTR fell ~3.3% intraday Monday (driving the 2.1x volume spike) after President Trump said the US is "working on a massive deal" to buy potash from Belarus at prices below what it currently pays Canada — a direct threat to Nutrien's core US potash-export economics, though the deal is explicitly still being negotiated, not signed. That headline risk sits alongside a mixed fundamental backdrop: National Bank downgraded NTR to sector perform on Aug 25, and a Sept 1 technical screen flagged the stock as overbought (RSI 72.3) after a ~15% one-month run, while RBC still reiterates an outperform rating ($85 PT, Aug 10) citing accelerated buybacks and sub-$60/tonne potash cash costs. The evidence doesn't resolve to a clear net read — a still-unconfirmed political threat to pricing power, set against continued constructive operating execution.
invalidation: Confirmation (or rejection) of a formal US-Belarus potash supply agreement, or a reversal of the current overbought technical setup.
